- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true if sentiment reverses.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use 14-day moving average of true prices as baseline for correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 range with no clear trend, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 20-day SMA of true prices as anchor.
